title: Felix: Optimizing Tensor Programs with Gradient Descent
problem: Existing search-based tensor program optimizers require hours or days to find high-performance implementations due to the exponentially large search space of possible tensor program optimizations.
motivation: Automatically discovering high-performance tensor program implementations across diverse hardware platforms is essential for deploying efficient deep neural networks.
method: Felix uses gradient descent instead of exhaustive search to find high-performance tensor programs faster. Rather than trying millions of different optimization combinations one-by-one, Felix calculates which direction improves performance most and adjusts the program accordingly. This works by treating program optimization as a mathematically smooth problem where you can calculate improvement directions (a property called differentiability), rather than as a discrete set of isolated options to search through.
key_novelty: Felix applies gradient descent (continuous optimization that calculates improvement directions) to tensor program optimization instead of exhaustively searching discrete options.
contributions: Felix system for gradient descent-based tensor program optimization
Approach to formulate tensor program optimization as a differentiable search problem
Significant speedup in discovering high-performance programs compared to existing search methods

metrics.speedup: search time reduction (hours/days to faster discovery)

primary_theme: accelerating tensor program optimization via gradient descent
